chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The Takbir (saying 'Allahu Akbar') in the obligatory prayer, in the five prayers, is ninety-five Takbirations, of which five are the Takbir of Qunut."

key_terms.اَلتَّكْبِيرُ: The act of saying 'Allahu Akbar' (God is Greater), a key ritual utterance in prayer.
key_terms.اَلْقُنُوتِ: Qunut, a supplication recited during the prayer, typically in the second rak'ah of Fajr or other prayers.
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةُ اَلْقُنُوتِ: The specific Takbiration associated with entering or performing Qunut.

ai.seo_question: How many Takbirations are there in the five daily obligatory prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the precise ritual structure of the five daily obligatory prayers, establishing a total of ninety-five Takbirations. It specifically highlights that five of these occur during the Qunut, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the distinct legal status and recitation of Qunut in the Fajr prayer. This count underscores the meticulous attention to ritual precision (detailed fiqh) characteristic of the Kufan scholarly tradition.
